column1: # Where each gloss in lex-la.tsv was read.
# lemma | pos | tgt | sources | quote | stands
# The gloss is the English word a Latin word is woven for, and the tooltip and
# the word page print it back: it is the claim every reader meets first. Every
# other claim the pack makes about a word names its entry — notes in
# la-notes.tsv, etymons in la-etymons.tsv, genders in la-genders.tsv — and the
# gloss did not until 2026-10-06. The only check on it had been a pass on
# 2026-10-02 asking whether the English word occurs anywhere in the headword's
# Lewis & Short entry, which is how camera, taught for "room" and in Lewis &
# Short only a vault, was found and withdrawn.
# On 2026-10-06 every row was read against Lewis & Short, from the Perseus
# text. A script drafted a quote for each row from the entry's own glosses,
# the italic English Lewis & Short gives a word, and every quote was read
# against its entry and checked verbatim against the entry's text. Where the
# first gloss holding the English word was a phrase or a citation's
# translation — aliēnus's "to be a stranger to a thing", exspectāre's "I must
# wait a year" — the quote is the gloss the word itself is given.
#   ls:<key>   Lewis & Short, by the entry's key in the Perseus text: no
#              macrons, j for a consonantal i, a digit for a homograph (dico2
#              to say, dico1 to dedicate), a verb by its first person (amo).
# A word Lewis & Short gives inside another entry cites both, its own entry
# first: falsus, sapiēns and mortuus are participles given under fallo, sapio
# and morior; lentē, celeriter, vērē and valdē adverbs given under lentus,
# celer, vērus and validus; salvē and valē under salveo and valeo. A noun cites
# the entries la-genders.tsv read its gender in, homographs and all.
# Blank where the quote holds the row's English word. Otherwise it names the
# word of the quote that stands for it, because the English word is not in the
# entry: Lewis & Short spells "gray", "neighbor" and "to-day", has no "doctor"
# but "physician", no "hello" before the word existed, and glosses some words
# by a near synonym. Twenty rows need one, and each is a reading of how near:
# canis for "hound" is "a dog", carō for "meat" is "flesh", paenula for "coat"
# "a woollen outer garment". The loosest was tunica for "coat", "an
# under-garment of the Romans worn by both sexes, a tunic", and it was
# withdrawn for paenula the same day: see WITHDRAWN in src/core/renames.ts.
# tests/tools/la-glosses.test.ts requires every row of lex-la.tsv to have a
# line here, every line to cite Lewis & Short, every quote to hold its English
# word or name the word standing for it, and every noun to cite the entry its
# gender was read in. It cannot tell a quote somebody copied from the entry
# from one somebody typed, nor an entry somebody read from one somebody named.
